title: Stan Kenton's "new minority" remark and Duke's "race riot" at the Graystone
summary: After Kenton's remark about white players, Duke fired up his band before a Detroit battle of jazz; Jones doubts Kenton meant it that way.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: He really knew how to agitate. Well, you know, it was some years back -- I hope this doesn't offend anybody -- but Stan Kenton -- the times I've been around Stan Kenton, he's been very nice to me, you know, a nice guy. But he made a statement. I think he just -- he didn't really mean it as what people made out of it, you know. He says, 'There's
a new minority --," this was after the jazz poll.
Yeah, I guess it was Downbeat. But then they took it to the New York Post, you know?
And so Duke and Stan Kenton were --
Wait a minute. The whole quote was there's a new minority and what's the rest of it?
The new minority was the white race he said, the white players.

Yeah. So there was a battle of jazz booked in Detroit, at the Graystone Ballroom, I think. And Duke got in front of the bus to agitate his players. He says, "We're not having a battle of jazz tonight. We're going to a race riot."
You know? And he fired the guys up.
You know? He really fired them up. I says, "Oh, man, he's --," but I don't think Kenton meant that, not that way, you know.
Because I've spent some time with Kenton since I've been out here, you know.
What have you done for him?
Well, it's just with the neophonic thing, you know, with Wes, and his inviting me to some of his sessions and things, you know, and he became ill for awhile, you know. But --
